text_blocks.snippet: A bruise, also known as ecchymosis, is typically diagnosed based on its appearance and location after an injury. A healthcare provider may also perform a physical exam, potentially using imaging tests like X-rays, ultrasounds, or MRI, especially if the bruise is severe or accompanied by other symptoms.
snippet_highlighted_words: typically diagnosed based on its appearance and location after an injury

list.title: 1. Visual Examination:
list.snippet: The most common way to diagnose a bruise is by observing its color, size, and location on the body. Bruises typically appear as reddish, bluish, or purplish patches on the skin, and they may be tender to the touch.

list.title: 2. Physical Examination:
list.snippet: A doctor will assess the extent of the injury, look for other signs of trauma, and palpate (feel) the area to check for tenderness and swelling.

list.title: 3. Imaging Tests:
list.snippet: In cases of severe bruising or when bone or joint injuries are suspected, imaging tests like X-rays, ultrasounds, or MRI may be used to rule out fractures, bone bruises, or other underlying injuries.

list.title: 4. Blood Tests:
list.snippet: If a person experiences frequent or unexplained bruising, a doctor may order blood tests to check for bleeding disorders or vitamin deficiencies.

list.title: Severe pain:
list.snippet: If the pain from a bruise is intense or not relieved by over-the-counter pain medication, it's important to seek medical advice.

list.title: Swelling:
list.snippet: Excessive swelling around the bruised area, especially if it worsens or doesn't subside, warrants medical evaluation.

list.title: Numbness or weakness:
list.snippet: If you experience numbness, tingling, or weakness in the bruised area, or if you lose function, consult a doctor.

list.title: Bruises that don't heal:
list.snippet: If a bruise doesn't start to fade within two weeks, or if it's accompanied by other concerning symptoms, it's best to get it checked out.

list.title: Frequent or unexplained bruising:
list.snippet: If you bruise easily or frequently, consult a doctor to rule out any underlying medical conditions.
Most bruises can be diagnosed based on visual assessment and physical examination.
Imaging tests are used to rule out more serious injuries like bone fractures or bone bruises.
Blood tests can help identify underlying bleeding disorders or other conditions causing easy bruising.
Seek medical attention for severe pain, excessive swelling, numbness, weakness, or bruises that don't heal or are accompanied by other concerning symptoms.
